title: PUBLIC INFORMATION MEETING
full_story:
The City of Flora will have a public information meeting on Monday, August 17th at 4:15 pm.  The city is pursuing funding through the Illinois Transportation Enhancement Program (ITEP) for proposed sidewalk improvements to create safer pedestrian routes to local schools and the industrial park.

Residents, parents, property owners, employees, and community members are encouraged to attend, learn about the proposed project, ask questions, and share input.

The city needs the community to show their support for the project.  The meeting will be at 4:15 pm on Monday, August 17th at Flora City Hall.

title: S.U.R.E. SYMPOSIUM
full_story:
The Clay County Health Department is collaborating with the Coalition Against Drug Abuse of Clay County, the Clay County Board, SIU School of Medicine, and Birth to Five Illinois to bring the second Substance Use Resource & Education Symposium or S.U.R.E Symposium to Clay County tomorrow.  Registration will begin at 8:30 am at the Oil Belt Christian Service Camp.

The goal of the S.U.R.E. Symposium is to bring together local agencies, experts, and community members to provide a safe space to learn about substance abuse prevention, recovery, and what happens after.

Speakers will be Liesl Wingert from the SIU School of Medicine, Shelly Kuhns, with Gentle Care Consultants, Andy Greer with the Gateway Foundation, Clay County States Attorney Phil Givens, and Clay County Sheriff’s Sgt Elam Lewis.

Lunch will be provided to the first 200 who register, and continuing education units are available.  Register by going to tinyurl.com/SURE2026 or use the QR code on the health department’s website.  This years symposium registration is being covered by the Clay County Board Opioid Settlement.

title: I57 FATALITIES
full_story:
25-year-old Madison Burton of Odin died in a crash on southbound I-57 three miles south of Dix Thursday night.

Jefferson County Coroner Roger Hayse pronounced Burton dead in the emergency room of Good Samaritan Hospital.  He says she was waiting in her car on the shoulder of the road for help to arrive to assist her in changing a flat tire.  Her car was apparently struck in the rear by a pickup truck that had left the roadway.

State Police have not released details on how the crash occurred, but indicated a semi truck was also involved.

Jefferson Fire Officials say the impact caused Burton’s car to be pushed off the shoulder and to overturn.  Burton had to be extricated by firemen.  She was later pronounced dead in the emergency room of the hospital.

The name of the driver of the pickup that struck Burton has not been released.

The crash was reported just after 10 Thursday night.  State Police say traffic had to be diverted around the scene for over 5 hours.

Friday morning just after 4 am Illinois State Police were called to a single vehicle accident with a fatality just south of the I 57, 70 split.

The 20-year-old female driver from Champaign County was pronounced dead at the scene.  The single-passenger vehicle skidded off the damp pavement and struck the guardrail. Effingham County Coroner Kim Rhodes said that there was very heavy rainfall in that area just prior to the crash.  Family members told Rhodes that the woman was headed to Atlanta, Georgia.

title: UPLAND GAME HUNTING PERMIT LOTTERY
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) reminds upland game hunters that applications are now being accepted for the 2026 free upland game hunting permit lottery and the controlled pheasant hunting program.  These programs provide opportunities to hunt at select state sites across Illinois this fall.

The free upland game hunting permit program offers lottery-assigned, no-cost hunting opportunities for wild upland game, including bobwhite quail, ring-necked pheasants and cottontail rabbits.  The controlled pheasant hunting program is a fee-based program that offers opportunities to hunt pen-reared ring-necked pheasants released at participating state sites.

Applications for the free upland game hunting permit lottery will be accepted through August 31st.  Hunters may select up to six hunt areas and four dates for each area using the online application.  Applicants may list the same hunt area multiple times to improve their chances of receiving preferred hunting dates.

Hunters can find participating sites, permit rules, application instructions and application status information on the IDNR Upland Game Hunting webpage.

The controlled pheasant hunting program includes three lottery drawings followed by a first-come, first-served permit period.  Youth permits primarily will be available during the first-come, first-served period, and additional wingshooting clinics are being added to select youth pheasant hunts.  A complete list of youth clinics will be announced at a later date.

Resident permits cost $35, and nonresident permits are $40.  Eleven Illinois state parks participate in the controlled pheasant hunting program.  Applications, program information and participating site details are available on the IDNR Controlled Pheasant Hunting webpage.

title: STATE FAIR FREE CONCERT
full_story:
Music fans are invited to experience an unforgettable night at the Illinois State Fair when legendary southern rock band 38 Special performs a FREE Grandstand concert on Monday, August 17th.  The concert will kick off with special guest Warrant.

“The Illinois State Fair should be an experience that every Illinois family can enjoy,” said Governor JB Pritzker.  “By offering a free Grandstand concert, discounted admission tickets and special fair food pricing, we are making it easier for more Illinois citizens to come together and create lasting memories at the Illinois State Fair.”

For more than five decades, 38 Special has brought their signature blast of guitar-driven southern rock to audiences around the world.  Known for their infectious blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks, the band has produced a long list of hits that have stood the test of time, including “Hold On Loosely,” “Caught Up in You,” “Rockin’ Into the Night,” “If I’d Been the One,” and “Second Chance.”  With over 20 million albums sold, 38 Special continues to tour nationwide, delivering high-energy performances that showcase their timeless sound and unmistakable style.  Their music remains a staple on classic rock radio, and their live shows continue to draw fans of all generations.

The FREE 38 Special concert takes place Monday, August 17th at the Illinois State Fair Grandstand.  Gates open at 7 pm and no ticket is required, but attendees must go through security screening prior to entering the Grandstand.

Admission is free for kids 12 and under every day of the fair.  On Monday, August 17th, senior citizens and scouts in uniform get free admission while general admission is $5.  Daily food deals are also available in the Reisch Pavilion and the Village of Cultures.

title: INDICTED IN FRANKLIN COUNTY MINE FIRE
full_story:
Four managers and supervisors of a Franklin County mine were indicted for failing to evacuate miners during an underground fire, conspiracy to obstruct investigators, and falsifying records.

69-year-old Ronald Dale Koontz of Hendersonville, Tennessee, 38-year-old Demitrios George Macropoulos of Buckeye, Arizona, 67-year-old Randy L. Nowland of Waltonville, Illinois, and 37-year-old Cory Taylor Humphrey of Prospect, Kentucky, were charged with multiple crimes related to an underground fire that occurred in the MC#1 Mine in Franklin County, in August 2021.

The indictment returned Tuesday charges all four with conspiring to defraud the US Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) by concealing the fire and other hazards at the mine and taking steps to interfere with the investigation of the fire and administration of safety-related orders in the aftermath of the fire.  The Indictment charges the defendants with keeping miners underground and continuing to mine coal for all or portions of three shifts while unsuccessfully fighting a fire.  The defendants are charged with failing to evacuate the mine and notify MSHA as required by mandatory safety standards under the Federal Mine Safety and Health Act.  Nowland and Humphrey are also charged under the Mine Act with falsification of records required to document mine hazards.  Koontz and Macropoulos are charged with obstruction of an MSHA proceeding for entering the mine in violation of an MSHA safety order withdrawing miners from the mine.  Koontz is further charged with obstruction for directing another supervisor to delete a record reflecting a telephone call he made.

A fifth conspirator and former mine manager, Brandon Timothy Parsons, pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud MSHA on August 28th, 2025 in a related criminal proceeding filed in August 2025.

Principal Deputy Assistant Attorney General Adam Gustafson of the Energy and Natural Resources Division says as Congress has long recognized, a strong, productive coal industry depends on miners who feel safe and trust that their leaders are not putting them at unnecessary risk.

“When people in positions of authority conceal deadly conditions and then cover up their actions, they put lives at risk and prevent federal authorities from doing the job the law requires them to do.  That kind of obstruction is unacceptable,” said US Attorney Steven D. Weinhoeft.  “These charges hold accountable those who chose to protect the company’s financial interests over the safety of the people they are obligated to protect.”

If convicted, the defendants each face possible incarceration.  If found guilty, a federal district court judge will determine any sentence after considering the US Sentencing Guidelines and other statutory factors.
